issues.title: Parallel perfect-HJ build + dense INNER builds up to 4M range
issues.hypothesis: The perfect HJ build runs serially inside PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize (physical_hash_join.cpp:1202-1207 -> PerfectHashJoinExecutor::BuildPerfectHashTable -> FullScanHashTable: ScanKeyColumn over all rows, then one data_collection.Gather per payload column, all on one thread). The regular HJ finalize is parallel (ScheduleFinalize). Measured A/B, warm, 8 threads, on near-identical data: lineitem JOIN part with p_partkey<=1048000 (range under MAX_BUILD_SIZE, so perfect HJ) took 153-175ms. The same query with p_partkey<=1049000 (just over the limit, so regular HJ + BF) took 102-125ms, 4 alternating pairs. In JSON profiles the perfect variant has LOWER join CPU (0.20s vs 0.39s) but 57ms HIGHER latency (0.180 vs 0.123s). The serial build is pure wall-clock loss. So today the perfect HJ makes every 0.5M-1M-row dense build slower. That is also why CanDoPerfectHashJoin cannot be opened further: INNER joins with range >1M are rejected even when dense (line 120-121, `!PropagatesBuildSide(op.join_type) ||`). q14 builds part (2M dense keys p_partkey 1..2M, payload p_type VARCHAR) with a regular HJ: HASH_JOIN 0.58s operator time / 1.08s CPU vs a 773k-row probe. This is the biggest operator in q14 (171ms).
issues.plan: Step 1, parallel build: in PerfectHashJoinExecutor (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp) keep the serial ScanKeyColumn + TemplatedFillSelectionVectorBuild (duplicate check, cheap int work). Time it first with a local timer to confirm the gather dominates. Then build a slot->tuple mapping and split the payload Gather (FullScanHashTable lines 190-199) into tasks over contiguous SLOT ranges aligned to 64. Validity words are written non-atomically by Gather, so tasks must never share a validity word. Schedule them from PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize the same way ScheduleFinalize / HashJoinFinalizeEvent (physical_hash_join.cpp ~line 528) schedules HashJoinFinalizeTask: e.g. a PerfectHashJoinFinalizeEvent whose tasks each call executor.GatherRange(begin,end). Keep the serial path when the build has fewer than ~64k rows. The duplicate/fallback decision stays serial and before scheduling, so the fallback to ScheduleFinalize is unchanged. Do the col_mask.Combine(bitmap_build_idx) per range as well (or keep it serial: it is word-wise and cheap). Step 2: in CanDoPerfectHashJoin, drop the `!PropagatesBuildSide(op.join_type) ||` term, so INNER joins also qualify for range <= MAX_DENSE_BUILD_SIZE (4M) when ht.Count()*2 >= range+1. Validate: rerun the p_partkey<=1048000 vs <=1049000 A/B (the perfect variant should now be at least as fast), then q14 and q13 (RIGHT perfect HJ on 1.5M customer) in the bench. Correctness: compare against SET disabled_optimizers / a variant with a hash-forcing extra condition, including NULL payloads and VARCHAR payloads, INNER and RIGHT.
issues.expected_gain: q14 -15..-25% (2M dense part build becomes a parallel perfect HJ; join CPU roughly halves per the A/B). q13 a few % if its RIGHT perfect build is latency-bound. Any template with a 0.3-1M-row dense build (perfect today) gains up to ~50ms of latency. Geomean -1.5..-3%.
issues.generality: Every FK join against a dense-key dimension (part, customer, supplier, date dims, surrogate keys) at larger scale factors. It removes a serial phase that grows linearly with build size. Could get slower: dense builds whose probe side is tiny. A 4M-slot perfect table is allocated and gathered where the regular HJ would also build 4M entries, so the memory is similar. Sparse perfect HJ stays excluded by the 50% density gate (a prior 8M sparse attempt regressed).
issues.risk: Medium. Concurrent Gather into shared dictionary vectors must not race on validity words or string data, so use slot-range partitioning. Event scheduling in Finalize must keep the perfect/regular fallback logic intact. If the payload gather is not the dominant serial cost, step 1 gains little; the implementer should time it first.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen2)

## State
- gen1 (r1-r16): accepted E0001 JoinDependent rule order (q19), E0002 contains() selectivity (q09), E0003 perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), E0005 BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), E0006 key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), E0007 exact bitmap BF, E0011 semi-join estimate, E0012 OR-of-ranges mask, E0014 FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), E0016 DELIM_GET-build BF (q22 -20%). Best 1.281x.
- gen2 r1+r2: E0017/E0018 (no CM on hash-join keys) RETIRED twice: hidden validation regressed. DEAD.
- gen2 r5: E0021 = bundle of E0019 (deliminate SEMI) + E0020 (exact BF through CM offset) ACCEPTED. Each had been retired alone in r3/r4.
- gen2 r6: E0022 exact-BF small-range floor ACCEPTED (geomean -9.9%).
- gen2 r7: E0023 ANTI deliminator ACCEPTED (q22 -22..-29%, geomean -2.8%). Best 1.518x.
- gen2 r8: DISPATCHED "Parallel perfect-HJ build + dense INNER builds up to 4M range" (q14 target). If step 1 (parallel) alone shows nothing on the bench, step 2 (INNER dense) is what moves q14; they need each other.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this codebase. Treat them as strong measured priors, not landed code.
- .dbe/issues.md: the first 3 issues are stale (already landed). The "aggregate CM skip q13" issue is DEAD. The RIGHT_SEMI join filters issue landed in E0021.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Bundle verified wins.

## Key finding r8: the perfect HJ build is SERIAL and loses on latency
- PhysicalHashJoin::Finalize (physical_hash_join.cpp ~1202) calls BuildPerfectHashTable -> FullScanHashTable inline on one thread. The regular HJ finalize is parallel.
- A/B (lineitem x part, p_partkey<=1048000 perfect vs <=1049000 regular): perfect 153-175ms vs regular 102-125ms. Join CPU 0.20 vs 0.39s, but latency +57ms.
- CanDoPerfectHashJoin: MAX_BUILD_SIZE 1<<20; MAX_DENSE_BUILD_SIZE 1<<22, only for PropagatesBuildSide (RIGHT) and only if count*2 >= range.
- q14 (171ms): part 2M dense build, regular HJ 0.58s operator time / 1.08s CPU; lineitem scan 0.47s (60M -> 773k by shipdate). The part scan costs only 6ms.
- How to A/B a threshold without code changes: add a key-range predicate just under/over the limit.

## Measured r7
- q13 eager aggregation as a manual rewrite: only -4%. DEAD.
- q22 warm CPU breakdown is in the E0023 notes (now solved).
- HJ build cost: a 7.2M-row orders build with a tiny probe = 0.91s CPU, ~126ns/row (q03/q05/q09 orderkey HJs). A possible target (radix-partition-local inserts), unverified. Prior "HJ prefetch no gain".
- dbe-tool profile output looks COLD. Use the warm JSON trick.
- No PK/UNIQUE constraints in the schema.
- q05: the l_orderkey BF (455k keys over a 60M range) stays hashed. Raising the cap gives only ~10% fewer rows. Low value.

## How to get full operator timings
- dbe-tool sql "<warm q>; <warm q>; SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <q>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"|"operator_cardinality"|"latency"|"Dynamic Filters"'. /tmp is NOT readable. Compare "latency" too: CPU alone hides serial phases.

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except an exact BF through the offset on cond 0 (E0021). A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.
- Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter caps EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE=1<<22, MAX_RANGE=1<<32. Hashed BF: 12 bits/key.
- PushRangeSetFilter (gap-split ranges) only for 50 < keys <= 3200.

## Measurement lessons
- The first 2-3 runs of a query in a process are slow (~2x warm-up). Alternate A/B/A/B.
- Do NOT wrap in count(*): it changes the plan. Use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables, no $(...).
- Bench noise is ±10-20% per template (q19, q08, q03, q14 worst).
- In long bench sequences q18 is ~10% slower after q09/q13 (artifact).

## Profile snapshot (r8): q13 572, q18 551, q09 478, q05 253, q03 196, q07 192, q08 179, q16 174, q04 173, q14 171, q17 146, q22 110, q19 105, q02 65. Geomean 198.3.
- q13: inner agg 3.08s CPU, orders scan 2.65s (NOT LIKE), decompress/compress 0.80s, RIGHT HJ 0.58s.
- q03: lineitem scan 2.24s CPU, HJ on l_orderkey 0.75s.
- q18: 15M-group agg dominates (exhausted).

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation: ~0% or worse.
- Large perfect HA: real q13 gain (-20%), but the bench flags q18 each time (artifact). Possible retry: a shared table with striped updates.
- FSST DecompressVector path is not hot.

## Next candidates
1. (dispatched r8) parallel perfect-HJ build + INNER dense.
2. HJ build throughput on large regular builds (126ns/row). Measure the sink vs finalize split first.
3. q07/q08 not analysed warm.
4. q07: gate the offset BF when the scan already has a selective BF (only if q07 gets flagged).
5. MARK delim joins (IN/EXISTS in OR) via the deliminator: check the NULL semantics.

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. In release, CM on a join fires only if est. build >= 1M rows and join/build ratio <= 8.
- Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp. Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp: SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter (SEMI+ANTI now), ConvertNotDistinctToEqual, SubqueryIsSimple.
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters. NDF conds are skipped. DELIM_GET build => build_side_has_filter.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp (CanDoPerfectHashJoin :66, FullScanHashTable :152). HashJoinFinalizeTask in physical_hash_join.cpp ~:528. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp.
- Noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%; q04 ~20%; q08/q17 ±5-15%.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.
